Name: About this sheet
Content: All-in-one Qualtrics prospecting resource built from 382 real emails that booked meetings, plus research from Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, and Outreach. Filter the Resource_Type column: Framework Overview = pick your scenario; Email Template = copy/paste body; Real Example = filled-in winner from the source doc; Subject Line rows = subject templates, examples, and rules; Swap-In Bank = openers/proof/CTAs to remix; Source Email = all 382 original winners categorized.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Recommended flow: 1) Pick framework via Framework Overview. 2) Copy the Email Template. 3) Model your fill-ins on the Real Example. 4) Pick a Subject Line Template. 5) Check the Checklist rows before sending.

Name: F1 You Already Use Us (Expansion)
Use_When: Account is already a Qualtrics customer; you want a new stakeholder/team
Notes_Why_It_Works: 61 of 382 winners (16%). Heaviest: Higher Ed, Healthcare, Foodservice. Converts cold intro to warm in sentence 1 - the company already vouches for you; "what's new (AI)" gives a reason to talk now.

Name: F2 Reconnect / New POC
Use_When: Prior conversation, lapsed deal, or you inherited the account
Notes_Why_It_Works: 60 of 382 (16%) - HIGHEST REPLY RATE. Heaviest: Healthcare (19), Education, Gov. "Based on my notes you spoke with [X] in [year]" proves homework; "Qualtrics has changed since" makes a no-pressure reason to talk.

Name: F3 Role + Peer Proof (Cold)
Use_When: Genuinely cold/net-new; you know their role + relevant named peers
Notes_Why_It_Works: 135 of 382 (35%) - largest bucket. Heaviest: Healthcare, Gov SLG, Education. Three beats: relevant to your role -> proof via named peers -> low-commitment ask.

Name: F4 Trigger Strike (Intent/Signal)
Use_When: They did something: demo view, content view, pricing request, new role, published initiative, inbound request
Notes_Why_It_Works: 71 of 382 (19%). Heaviest: Healthcare (33), Life Sciences (11). Timely + earned; shortest emails; fastest conversions. Pair with same-day phone call.

Name: F5 Borrowed Trust (Referral/On-site)
Use_When: Someone can vouch for you (referral/internal sponsor) or your AE is in their area
Notes_Why_It_Works: 55 of 382 (14%). Heaviest: Gov SLG (16), K-12 (15). Transfers a third party's credibility instantly; on-site adds scarcity.

Name: Open by naming the relationship, not yourself
Content: Top openers: "I'm on the Qualtrics team supporting [Company]" / "I support the [Company] + Qualtrics relationship alongside [Colleague]" / "Reaching out on behalf of the [Company] account team." Most-repeated phrase in dataset: "account team here at Qualtrics".
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: One specific true detail in line 1
Content: A role, prior conversation, trigger, new-role congrats, or referrer. Never "I hope this email finds you well".
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: Proof through named peers
Content: "...your peers including companies like Citi, AMEX, and JPMC" / "...life sciences orgs such as Boston Scientific, Johnson & Johnson and Roche".
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: A reason to talk NOW
Content: Almost always "what's new" (AI / new capabilities in last 12 months) or a deadline (renewal, RFP, license sunset).
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: One small specific soft ask
Content: #1 CTA in the data: "Would you be open to a 20-minute introductory call sometime next week?"
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: Under ~130 words
Content: 60% of winners land in the 76-130 word band; only 20% exceed 130.
Notes_Why_It_Works: From analysis of all 382 winners

Name: Rule 1 - Short wins
Content: <=4 words for cold, <=6 for warm. Gong/30MPC (85M emails): 1-4 words, shorter = higher open. Lavender (500M emails): sweet spot 36-50 chars (~4-7 words). Source doc median: 4 words / 27 chars.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 2 - all lowercase
Content: All four sources favor all-lowercase (proper nouns excepted) - reads like a note from a colleague, not a campaign.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 3 - Internal camouflage
Content: Biggest idea from Gong/30MPC: mirror how the buyer's coworkers email them - short noun phrases like "trial delays", "hiring ops", "2024 forecasts". Cold subjects should NOT contain "Qualtrics"; warm ones may.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 4 - Never sell or buzzword in the subject
Content: Gong: pitching reduces replies by up to 57%. Do not say "AI" or use buzzwords in the subject - save it for the body.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 5 - Personalize
Content: Outreach/Lavender: personalized subjects lift opens 22-50% (deep personalization 40%+). Reference THEIR company, role, or event - not your product.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 6 - No "?" or numbers in COLD
Content: Lavender: questions -56% and numbers -46% opens in cold. (Outreach finds both help in warm/nurture - so questions/numbers are OK for F1/F2/F5 warm threads only.)
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Rule 7 - Subject + first line work as a pair
Content: 30MPC: the subject sets up the opener; don't waste the subject repeating the first line.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Benchmark
Content: Lavender: good cold open rate = 25-40%; excellent = 40%+; below 15% = subject line or deliverability problem. A/B test ONE variable on a 20-30 prospect split.
Notes_Why_It_Works: Sources: Lavender, Gong, 30MPC, Outreach (see Sources rows)

Name: Subject strategy - F1 You Already Use Us (Expansion)
Content: Warm - relationship is the hook; "Qualtrics/[Company]" looks like a real internal thread; connectors (<>, |, +) reinforce it. Questions OK.
Notes_Why_It_Works: A/B: "[Company] <> Qualtrics" (relationship) vs "quick one on [Company]'s setup" (curiosity). Strongest single performer: "Consolidation" - one internal-sounding noun.
